description: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of token counts across seven distinct text categories used in the training of large language models for the Sámi language, as referenced in the paper “Towards a More Inclusive AI: Progress and Perspectives in Large Language Model Training for the Sámi Language.” The vertical axis, labeled “Tokens (K),” represents the number of tokens in thousands, ranging from 0 to 10,000 with major tick marks at intervals of 2,000. The horizontal axis, labeled “Categories,” lists the text domains: Administrative, Religion, Non-fiction, Fiction, Law, News, and Blogs. Each category is represented by a single vertical bar, with the exact token count labeled above each bar in blue font. The “News” category dominates with 10,584K tokens, followed by “Administrative” at 6,472K, and “Non-fiction” at 1,889K. The remaining categories have significantly fewer tokens: “Religion” (652K), “Fiction” (387K), “Law” (354K), “Blogs” (32K), and an unlabeled gray bar (1,626K) positioned between “News” and “Blogs,” which may represent an aggregated or placeholder category. The bars are not sorted by magnitude, and the “Blogs” category is notably the smallest, suggesting a severe imbalance in data representation across domains.
